# Behavioral Discrepancy Rules

This reference defines the 10 behavioral rules evaluated by `scripts/analyze-behavior.ts` and `scripts/typespec-validator.ts` when comparing raw wire HTTP exchanges against an in-memory version-projected ARM TypeSpec `Program`.

| Rule ID                      | Default Severity       | What It Detects                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `LRO-UNDECLARED`             | `blocking`             | TypeSpec models the operation as synchronous (`getLroMetadata` is undefined), but live service returns HTTP `202`, emits `Azure-AsyncOperation` / `Location` / `Operation-Location` polling headers, or returns `200`/`201` with non-terminal `properties.provisioningState`.                 |
| `LRO-HEADER-DRIFT`           | `blocking` / `warning` | TypeSpec models the operation as an LRO, but an async live response (`202` or non-terminal `provisioningState`) omits polling headers completely (`blocking`), or returns different polling headers (`Azure-AsyncOperation` vs `Location`) than declared on that response status (`warning`). |
| `LRO-FINAL-STATE-DRIFT`      | `blocking`             | On async `POST` actions, TypeSpec `LroMetadata.finalStateVia` (`location` vs `azure-async-operation`) disagrees with where the live service actually delivers the terminal action payload.                                                                                                    |
| `STATUS-CODE-DRIFT`          | `blocking`             | Live service returns a non-error HTTP status code (e.g., `202` instead of `200`, or `204` instead of `200` on `DELETE`) not declared in the TypeSpec operation return union.                                                                                                                  |
| `SCHEMA-RESPONSE-DRIFT`      | `warning`              | TypeSpec wire validator reports schema discrepancies on the live response body (scalar/model type mismatch, missing required `Lifecycle.Read` property, closed enum/union violation, union casing mismatch, or a bodyless declared 2xx status code returning an undocumented JSON body).      |
| `SCHEMA-REQUEST-REJECTED`    | `warning`              | Request payload passed TypeSpec `Lifecycle.Create`/`Update` validation with 0 errors, yet the live RP rejected it with HTTP `400 BadRequest`—indicating undocumented server constraints (`@minLength`, `@pattern`, requiredness, or allowed SKU/union combinations).                          |
| `ROUNDTRIP-MUTABILITY-DRIFT` | `warning`              | Non-`@secret` writable properties (visible in both Create/Update and Read) sent in `PUT` are absent from the terminal `PUT` or subsequent `GET` resource representation without `@visibility(Lifecycle.Create, Lifecycle.Update)`.                                                            |
| `PAGEABLE-CONTRACT-DRIFT`    | `blocking` / `warning` | TypeSpec declares `@list` / `@pageItems` paging while service returns a bare array or different wrapper (`blocking`), or service returns `{ value, nextLink }` pagination while TypeSpec models a non-paged `GET` (`warning`).                                                                |
| `ERROR-ENVELOPE-DRIFT`       | `blocking` / `warning` | Live 4xx/5xx response does not conform to ARM OData v4 `{ error: { code, message } }` (`blocking`), or the TypeSpec operation omits an `@error` response (`warning`).                                                                                                                         |
| `PROVISIONING-STATE-DRIFT`   | `warning`              | Terminal polled resource state ends with a `properties.provisioningState` outside ARM RPC terminal values (`Succeeded`, `Failed`, `Canceled`).                                                                                                                                                |
